releases.body:
Contributor-facing release. The shipped `src/` and `dist/` are byte-identical to v1.5.1, so upgrading changes nothing at runtime.

## Changed

- **Bun 1.3.14 is the development runtime.** Tests, coverage, the mutation contract, smokes, benchmarks, `verify`, `check` and `bundle` run under Bun. Install with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; `bun.lock` replaces `package-lock.json`.
- **The `npx` installer stays on Node.** CI keeps a `Node installer (npx path)` job on Node 18, the `engines` floor. The Node 18/20/22/24 unit-test matrix is gone.
- **Mutation contract:** a mutant only counts as killed when a test really fails, and each run stops at the first failure. One old mutant never compiled; it now does, and is killed.
- **Audit:** `bun audit --prod --audit-level=high` replaces `npm audit`.
- **Windows is not supported.** The Windows CI job is gone and the docs say so.

Full details in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sblattj/opencode-goal-pro-max-complete-plugin/blob/v1.5.2/CHANGELOG.md).

**Use this instead of v1.5.0.** The v1.5.0 bundles were built from a stale install, so `dist/` carried `zod` 4.4.3 instead of the lockfile's 4.6.7. That undid the 1.4.1 security update (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5, high).

Rebuilt from a clean `npm ci` with the pinned Bun 1.3.14. No other change. See the [v1.5.0 notes](https://github.com/sblattj/opencode-goal-pro-max-complete-plugin/releases/tag/v1.5.0) for forced compaction, the feature these releases add.

> **Use [v1.5.1](https://github.com/sblattj/opencode-goal-pro-max-complete-plugin/releases/tag/v1.5.1) instead.** This build carried `zod` 4.4.3, undoing the 1.4.1 security update.

Goal sessions now compact themselves. OpenCode never auto-compacts a model that reports `limit.context: 0`, so a long goal on such a model kept growing (638,078 tokens in the case that prompted this).

**Added: forced compaction, on by default at 200,000 tokens**

- `--compact-at <n>` and `compactAtTokens` set the threshold; `0` turns it off. It applies on every model, so a 1M-window model also compacts at 200k unless you raise it.
- Checked after every finished step, so one long turn is caught mid-turn. The idle check is the backstop.
- Never two compactions for one crossing. On a model with a real `limit.context`, the host's own check gets one step first.
- A failed compaction does not block the goal: the plugin deletes the failed compaction message, because the host would otherwise re-run it on later prompts.
- Bounded: 3 failed requests stop forcing until the next compaction, and forcing is held when two compactions in a row leave the context over the threshold.
- Goal sessions only. Forcing never pauses or stops a goal.

**Added: `npm run smoke:forced-compaction`**, which runs the feature against a real OpenCode host with a mock model.

Checked against OpenCode 1.19.0 (running) and the v1.19.5 source. Full details in `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/reference.md`.

- **Fixed: context fullness no longer stops a goal or tells it to wrap up.** On 1.4.0 a goal with 7.2M of 100M tokens spent and 18m of 8h elapsed paused with "budget wrap-up requested" because peak context reached 80% of the model's 128,000-token window. OpenCode compacts the session on its own when context fills, so context is not a budget. The `context window reached` stop, the context branch of the 80% wrap-up, the "context token(s) remaining" warning and the `context_remaining` line in the continuation prompt are gone. Token spend (`maxTokens`) and the clock (`maxDurationMs`) keep both their 80% wrap-up and their hard stop.
  - **A wrap-up names its budget.** The stop reason is `token budget wrap-up requested` or `time budget wrap-up requested`, and the prompt opens "Token budget limit near" or "Time budget limit near".
  - **Status and panel show current context.** `/goal status` and the sidebar show the latest message's context, which drops on compaction, instead of a lifetime high-water mark. The status label is `Context:` and says where the window size came from: `configured (--context-window)` or `auto (host catalog: <provider>/<model>)`.
  - **The auto-detected window prefers `limit.input`** when the model reports one, as OpenCode's own overflow check does (checked against OpenCode v1.19.4 `session/overflow.ts`).
  - **`contextWindowTokens` and `--context-window` are display only.** Still accepted; they no longer stop or nudge anything.
- **Security: bundled `zod` updated from 4.4.3 to 4.6.7** (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5, high).

- **Changed: a goal stops only when you stop it, when it finishes, when a budget runs out, or when the model is genuinely hard-blocked.** Every other automatic stop now records what happened and keeps going. `docs/reference.md` has a single "When a goal stops" section.
  - **Compaction is not a human.** OpenCode writes a user-role message for each compaction (a `compaction` part, then a synthetic "Continue if you have next steps" text). The plugin counted those as human turns, so with `noInterruptOnUserMessage: false` (the default before 1.2.0) every compaction paused the goal with "user intervention". `isHostSyntheticUserMessage` now excludes them.
  - **Your messages steer, never pause.** `noInterruptOnUserMessage` is deprecated: accepted, ignored, always on. No more "Stopped: user intervention".
  - **Turn-ending host events end the turn, not the goal.** Permission rejections, aborted turns (Escape), provider errors and attachment-resolution errors are recorded and the goal continues after the cooldown. Repeated provider errors back off 5 s, 10 s, 20 s … up to 5 minutes.
  - **Loop brakes nudge instead of stopping.** Stalled compactions (no longer aborting the session), low-progress turns and tool-free turns add a "Stalled:" re-plan instruction to the next continuation, and the cooldown backs off exponentially (`minDelayMs × 2^strikes`, up to 64×). Format-validation and auto-continue failures keep retrying with backoff.
  - **New option `promptRetryWakeMs` (default `5000`).** A failed auto-continue prompt starts no turn, so no idle follows it; the plugin now retries on its own after this delay (or the backed-off cooldown, if longer).
  - **A rejected completion audit keeps the goal active** and sends the auditor's reason with the next continuation.
  - **Planning-only agents defer, not stop.** Under Plan the goal's clock freezes; it resumes under the next executing agent, with that agent's context.
  - **Restart keeps a running goal running.** A goal that was active before a plugin restart continues at the next idle; downtime does not count against its duration budget. A newer pause or halt in the lifecycle ledger still wins over a stale snapshot, and a goal rebuilt from the ledger alone still loads paused.
- **New: `/goal halt`**, the user's stop (an alias of `/goal pause`, resumable with `/goal resume`). `/goal status` suggests halt/resume/clear while a goal runs.
- **Removed: the `goal_pause` tool** (13 tools now). `update_goal` and the canonical update path refuse `status: "paused"` with `pause_user_only`. Pausing is user-only.
- **Changed: blocking is deterred.** `goal_block` and `[goal:blocked]` still work with a concrete blocker, but every prompt surface, tool description, the shipped skill and the docs now say that blocking stops the whole goal and is only for input that only you can give; a mid-goal message from you is steering, not a reason to block.
- **Unchanged:** budget ceilings, `/goal pause` and `/goal clear`, completion, queued/backgrounded goals, and the two-process persistence fences (`terminal persistence failed`, `continuation claim persistence failed`).
